doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Television schedule versus nightly stage show
summary: The weekly TV rehearsal routine compared with the repetitive Branson theatre show, and how TV left time for jazz gigs.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And this was basically an every-day, like a full time job for you, right?

Well now that I have been introduced to the Lawrence Welk stage show, I’m now working in the band at the theatre, I’ve discovered that it’s much, much harder to do a stage production than it is television. A television show — I did it for twenty-two years — and there was a different program every week. We would rehearse two days. One day was sound rehearsal and the other day was sound and video. Well it involved about nineteen hours totally for each weekly show. Well I’m doing this theatre thing now, and I’m playing five hours a day, six days a week. And it’s just like a Broadway show, like New York. I had never done anything like that before. Now I know how hard it is to adjust your mind to playing the same show, night after night. And it doesn’t change. The only time it changes is if we bring a different Welk singer in, they do it for a couple of weeks at a time. They change the singers, but they don’t change the Lennon Sisters, they don’t change Joanne Castle or we have the Cathcart brothers and the Lennon Daughters.
The Lennon Daughters. Gee, it must be like — to keep your concentration is probably —

But I’m playing in the orchestra besides doing my own thing for a couple of numbers in the show, I’m playing all the music and it’s the same show every night. And it’s going to be this way for eight or nine months. And it takes a lot of changing in my mind to try to adjust to all of this. Because we only worked two days out of the week when we were on television. And this allowed me to go out and play jazz music, other engagements. And that added the variety in my career that was needed. I don’t know whether I can last on this.
Are you living there now? In Branson?

I’m living in Branson. It’s only temporary, but I don’t know yet whether I’m going to continue on or not. But it’s going to be a matter of whether I can get used to this stage type production. Well I’ve always heard about these shows that are running ten years at a time. I’ve always thought, how do the musicians do that — play the same music all the time? © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
